references.text: This verse describes the first offering from Nahshon, son of Amminadab, with identical gifts: a silver plate weighing 130 shekels and a silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering. The same pattern is repeated for all the tribes.
Netanel's offering from the tribe of Issachar with the same gifts: a silver plate, a silver bowl, and fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
Eliab's offering from the tribe of Zebulun follows the same pattern with identical gifts.
Elisur's offering from the tribe of Reuben is described with the same gifts.
Selumiel from the tribe of Simeon brings the same offering.
Eljasaf from the tribe of Gad with an identical offering gift.
Elishama from the tribe of Ephraim brings the same gifts.
Gamliel from the tribe of Manasseh with identical offerings.
The shekel of the sanctuary is mentioned as the standard unit of weight, the same measurement used here.
The grain offering (mincha) of fine flour mixed with oil is described in detail in Leviticus.
Fine flour mixed with oil used in an offering context during the consecration of the priests.
